theme: Notch signalling to HES/HEY transcription and its restraint
story: The centre is canonical Notch signalling, in which the released intracellular domain (here NOTCH4 ICD as an example) enters the nucleus and drives transcription of HES/HEY bHLH repressors, with the hallmark Notch gene set capturing the same output. The negative-regulation term supplies the brakes that limit pathway activity. Together the cluster describes one signalling axis from receptor cleavage to target-gene transcription, plus its feedback control, used in cell-fate decisions.

theme: Microtubule-based organelle transport and dynamics in neurons
story: The core is motor-driven transport of organelles along microtubules, notably plus-end-directed movement and axonal delivery of mitochondria. Microtubule severing and depolymerisation terms describe remodelling of the tracks themselves, and lysosome size regulation reflects positioning and handling of lysosomes moved on these tracks. Protection of motor neurons from apoptosis is the physiological stake, since defects in axonal transport and microtubule dynamics (e.g. spastin, kinesin mutations) cause motor neuron degeneration.

theme: Neutral amino acid transporters and inherited aminoacidurias
story: The centre is plasma-membrane transport of neutral amino acids, especially glycine, proline and tryptophan, by SLC6A19, SLC6A20 and SLC36A2 in kidney and intestine. The disease entries describe what happens when these carriers fail: Hartnup disorder from SLC6A19 loss and iminoglycinuria/hyperglycinuria from SLC6A20 and SLC36A2 variants. The cluster as a whole covers renal and intestinal reabsorption of amino acids and its genetic disorders.

theme: Axon guidance by netrin, Slit-Robo and ephrin cues
story: The cluster centres on growth-cone guidance in the developing nervous system, built from the main cue-receptor systems: netrin/DCC attraction and UNC5 repulsion, Slit/Robo repulsion at the midline, and Eph/ephrin contact repulsion and growth-cone collapse. DSCAM and CHL1 interactions, axon fasciculation, commissural pathfinding and midline choice point recognition describe how these signals steer axons, while second-messenger, ABL and actin-bundle terms describe the downstream cytoskeletal machinery. Negative chemotaxis and chemokine-signalling regulation reflect the repulsive, chemotactic logic shared with other migratory cells.

theme: Erythrocyte gas exchange and small-molecule gas transport
story: The centre is red blood cell gas exchange: uptake of oxygen and release of carbon dioxide in the lungs and the reverse in tissues, mediated by haemoglobin, carbonic anhydrase and band 3. Carbon dioxide membrane transport, intracellular oxygen transport (e.g. myoglobin), nitric oxide transport and transepithelial ammonium transport extend this to other small gaseous molecules carried across membranes, partly by the same Rh/aquaporin-type channels. The cluster is about moving respiratory gases and related small solutes between tissues and blood.

theme: Peroxisomal and mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation of acyl-CoAs
story: The core is oxidation of fatty acyl-CoAs, with medium-chain fatty acid catabolism and acyl-CoA metabolism at the centre. Peroxisomal steps form a coherent sub-story: phytanate alpha-oxidation produces pristanate, which is then beta-oxidised by acyl-CoA oxidase-dependent peroxisomal beta-oxidation. Malonyl-CoA (the regulator of mitochondrial fatty acid entry) and succinyl-CoA catabolism round out the acyl-CoA metabolic network, so the whole cluster is about breaking down fatty acids for energy and clearing branched-chain lipids.

theme: Cation-chloride cotransport in renal salt and cell volume control
story: The centre is the SLC12 family of cation-coupled chloride cotransporters (NKCC, KCC), together with potassium channels and paracellular transport, which drive renal sodium reabsorption and set intracellular chloride. Hyperosmotic and hypotonic responses and anion homeostasis describe the second role of these transporters in cell volume regulation. The disease entries show the consequences: SLC12A1 loss causes Bartter syndrome (renal salt wasting), and SLC12A6 (KCC3) loss causes corpus callosum agenesis with neuropathy.

theme: Endosome-Golgi-lysosome membrane trafficking and retrograde transport
story: The core is retrograde transport from early and late endosomes back to the trans-Golgi network and from the Golgi to the ER, the routes that recycle sorting receptors and resident proteins. Forward Golgi-to-endosome transport, lysosomal protein targeting and lysosome vesicle biogenesis describe the complementary anterograde route that delivers hydrolases via mannose-6-phosphate receptors. Endosome organisation, vesicle fusion, membrane docking, endosome-to-plasma membrane recycling and vesicular cholesterol transport supply the shared machinery, making this one picture of the endolysosomal trafficking network.

theme: Lysosomal glycan catabolism and lysosomal storage disorders
story: The centre is the lysosome and its hydrolases that degrade oligosaccharides and glycoconjugates, including hexosaminidases, neuraminidase and mannosidases. Glucosamine-containing compound, chitin and mannose metabolism describe the sugar substrates these enzymes cleave, while lysosomal enzyme secretion and lysosomal proteins describe enzyme delivery. The disease entries (HEXA/HEXB GM2 gangliosidoses, NEU1 sialidosis) show the storage disorders that follow when a step fails.

theme: MECP2-centred neuronal gene regulation and Rett syndrome
story: The core is MECP2, the methyl-CpG binding protein whose loss causes Rett syndrome: its regulation, its control of neuronal receptors, channels and transcription factors, and disease variants that lose binding to 5hmC-DNA or the NCoR/SMRT corepressor with its HDACs. The neuronal RNA-binding module (ELAVL3, CPEB3, YBX1) and negative regulation of cytoplasmic translation add the post-transcriptional layer of neuronal gene control. Touch, proprioception and calcium channel regulation are neuronal functions disrupted in this setting, so the cluster centres on epigenetic and translational control of neuron function.

theme: Vascular smooth muscle tone and blood pressure regulation
story: The centre is control of vascular smooth muscle contraction and relaxation, which sets arterial tone. Endothelin and catecholamines drive constriction, while eNOS (including NOSIP-mediated trafficking) produces nitric oxide that triggers cGMP synthesis and relaxation; actin-based movement terms reflect the contractile apparatus. Renal sodium excretion and urine volume add the kidney's contribution to blood pressure, giving an overall picture of cardiovascular and renal blood pressure homeostasis.

theme: Neurotrophin Trk receptor signalling to MAPK, PI3K and CREB
story: The centre is neurotrophin receptor signalling: NGF/TRKA and NTF3/NTRK3 activation, including ligand-independent TRKA activation. Downstream branches follow the classic routes, through RAS to ERK, ERK5 and p38 MAPK and through PI3K to AKT. These converge on CREB phosphorylation and NGF-stimulated transcription, so the cluster describes how neurotrophins drive gene expression for neuronal survival and differentiation.

theme: Mitotic and meiotic chromosome segregation and cell division
story: The core is the mechanics of cell division: centrosome maturation and duplication, spindle assembly via Ran, TPX2/Aurora A, NuMA, EML4/NUDC and NEK kinases, kinetochore attachment and the spindle checkpoint, and sister chromatid cohesion through cohesin loading and centromeric protection. Meiosis-specific terms (synaptonemal complex, programmed double-strand breaks and recombination, chiasmata, cohesion, polar body extrusion, spermatogenesis) form a parallel arm that uses the same segregation machinery. Exit steps (cleavage furrow, septins, formins, ESCRT abscission and nuclear envelope resealing) complete division, while CENPA deposition, SUMOylation of replication proteins and sister-chromatid repair keep the genome ready to be segregated.

theme: tRNA and rRNA modification, aminoacylation and translational fidelity
story: The centre is tRNA maturation: 5'-leader removal, nuclear processing and many chemical modifications (methylation, pseudouridylation, wybutosine at G37, t6A, wobble uridine thiolation and guanine modification) in both cytosol and mitochondria. Cytosolic and mitochondrial tRNA aminoacylation charges the matured tRNAs, and rRNA base methylation, mRNA pseudouridylation and ADAR editing extend the same modification logic to other RNAs. Translational fidelity and termination are the payoff, while tRNA-derived small RNAs are a by-product, so the cluster as a whole is about preparing accurate decoders for protein synthesis.

theme: RIG-I/MDA5 and TLR3 signalling to IRF3 and type I interferon
story: The centre is cytosolic sensing of viral dsRNA by RIG-I (DDX58) and MDA5 (IFIH1), together with endosomal TLR3, which converge on TBK1/IKKε to phosphorylate IRF3 and IRF7. Those factors induce type I interferon, and the cluster includes positive regulation of interferon signalling and antiviral defence as the outputs. Negative regulators of DDX58/IFIH1 provide the brakes, making this a complete antiviral innate immune circuit.

theme: Thyroid hormone synthesis, sulfation donors and selenium handling
story: The centre is thyroid hormone production: iodide uptake, H2O2 generation for thyroid peroxidase, regulation of hormone generation and thyroid hormone transport. Selenium metabolism to H2Se feeds the selenoprotein deiodinases that activate and inactivate thyroid hormone. PAPS synthesis and transport and purine nucleoside bisphosphate metabolism describe the sulfate donor used to sulfate hormones and other substrates, with PAPSS2 deficiency causing a skeletal dysplasia, so the cluster loosely joins hormone synthesis with its trace-element and sulfation support.

theme: p53-mediated DNA damage response, cell cycle arrest, senescence
story: The core is TP53: its activation by phosphorylation, its control of degradation through MDM2 and COP1, and its transcription of DNA repair genes. Responses to X-rays and gamma radiation are the triggering DNA damage, while CDK inhibition and cell-cycle genes describe the resulting arrest. Replicative senescence is the long-term outcome, and MASTL-driven mitotic progression is the opposing cell-cycle force, so the cluster is about how genotoxic stress halts proliferation.

theme: TNFR1 and TLR signalling to NF-kappaB via ubiquitination
story: The centre is NF-kappaB activation downstream of TNFR1 and TLR7/8/9, where IRAK1 and the TNFR1 complex recruit the IKK complex. Linear polyubiquitination (by LUBAC) and SUMOylation of immune proteins are the modifications that assemble and tune these signalling complexes, and positive and negative regulation of NF-kappaB activity describe its control. TNFR1-induced proapoptotic signalling is the alternative outcome when NF-kappaB survival signalling fails, giving one picture of inflammatory signal decisions between survival and death.

theme: Initiation and checkpoint control of S-phase DNA replication
story: The centre is cell-cycle DNA replication: origin initiation and its positive and negative regulation during S phase. E2F1 targets supply the replication genes switched on at the G1/S transition. The replication checkpoint and intra-S damage checkpoint ensure replication stops when DNA is damaged or stalled, making this a coherent picture of controlled genome duplication.

theme: Non-vesicular lipid transfer and phospholipid hydrolysis
story: The centre is intermembrane lipid transfer by lipid transfer proteins carrying phospholipids, glycosphingolipids and ceramide 1-phosphate between membranes. Glycerophospholipid catabolism and the hydrolysis of lysophospholipids (LPC, LPE) describe turnover of the same lipids. A2E biosynthesis, a toxic retinoid-phosphatidylethanolamine adduct that builds up in the retina, is a disease-linked product of this lipid handling, so the cluster as a whole is about moving and breaking down membrane lipids.

theme: Metallothionein and MTF1 response to heavy metals
story: The centre is MTF1-driven induction of metallothioneins, which bind zinc, copper, cadmium and other metals. Responses to cadmium, mercury, zinc, copper, iron, cobalt and selenium describe the range of metal stresses that engage this system, and cadmium transport and detoxification are its protective output. The cluster as a whole is a heavy-metal sensing and detoxification programme.

theme: Cellular senescence and Polycomb silencing of CDKN2A
story: The centre is cellular senescence: oncogene- and oxidative-stress-induced and stress-induced premature senescence, in which cells permanently leave the cycle. The two BTM modules supply the chromatin control: Polycomb PRC1 (BMI1) and PRC2 accessory AEBP2 silence the CDKN2A (p16/ARF) locus to keep cells proliferating, opposed by USP16. Negative regulation of G0-to-G1 transition and of stress kinase signalling describe the proliferative and stress-signal sides, so the cluster is about the decision between continued division and senescent arrest.

theme: Base excision, alkylation reversal and DNA demethylation repair
story: The core is DNA damage reversal and base excision repair: direct alkylation reversal by MGMT and ALKBH2/3, glycosylase recognition of damaged pyrimidines, AP site resolution and single-strand break repair. NEIL3-mediated unhooking of interstrand cross-links (and its defect) extends glycosylase-based repair to cross-links. TET-driven oxidation and TDG excision of 5-methylcytosine reuse the same base excision machinery for active DNA demethylation and CpG island gene activation, uniting the cluster around base-level DNA chemistry.

theme: TCR signalling in T cell activation and differentiation
story: The centre is T cell receptor signalling through ITK and PKC, which drives T cell activation and differentiation. Thymic positive selection and differentiation of CD8 alpha-beta and gamma-delta T cells describe the developmental outcomes, and the IL2/IL7/TCR network adds the cytokine signals that support survival and expansion. Together they describe how T cells develop and become activated.

theme: LDL receptor-mediated cholesterol uptake and its regulation
story: The centre is LDL clearance by receptor-mediated endocytosis and LDL receptor particle metabolism, which supply cells with cholesterol. Negative regulation of receptor recycling, positive regulation of receptor and lysosomal protein catabolism and limited pinocytosis describe how receptors such as LDLR are diverted to lysosomes (via PCSK9 or IDOL). LXR (NR1H2/NR1H3) induction of IDOL to limit cholesterol uptake and overall sterol homeostasis explain why: the cluster is about the feedback loop that matches cholesterol uptake to cellular need.

theme: RIG-I-like receptor antiviral signalling to interferon and NF-kB
story: The centre is RIG-I-like receptor signalling, in which cytosolic sensors detect viral dsRNA and signal through MAVS. Downstream branches activate IRF7 via TRAF6 and NF-kB via FADD/RIP1 and caspase-8/10, together producing type I interferon and inflammatory gene expression. Positive regulation of interferon signalling and negative regulators of DDX58/IFIH1 tune the response, forming one antiviral innate immune pathway.

theme: Oxidised LDL handling and macrophage foam cell formation
story: The centre is macrophage response to oxidised LDL, leading to foam cell differentiation in atherosclerosis. Phosphatidylcholine catabolism and regulation of phospholipid catabolism describe the phospholipases (such as Lp-PLA2) that process oxidised lipoprotein phospholipids, and lipoprotein transport describes lipid movement. The cluster as a whole describes lipoprotein lipid processing that drives early atherosclerotic lesions.

theme: Tryptophan-kynurenine pathway and NAD(P) metabolism
story: The core is tryptophan catabolism through kynurenine, which feeds de novo NAD+ synthesis, joined by nicotinate (Preiss-Handler) metabolism, NADP+ synthesis and NAD+ consumption. Oxidoreductase regulation fits the redox role of these cofactors. Mitochondrial ATP/ADP transport and phosphocreatine metabolism extend this to cellular energy currency, so the cluster loosely centres on making and using the cell's redox and energy cofactors.

theme: Phase I/II xenobiotic and drug detoxification metabolism
story: The centre is xenobiotic metabolism, with phase I oxidation by cytochromes P450 (CYP1A2 N-hydroxylation, CYP2E1 reactions, oxidative demethylation) and flavin monooxygenases. Phase II methylation (TPMT) and drug handling such as paracetamol ADME describe conjugation and clearance, while mycotoxins, phenylpropanoids, monoterpenoids, benzene compounds and nitrogen compounds are the varied substrates. FMO3 (trimethylaminuria) and TPMT deficiency show the clinical cost of losing these enzymes; the cluster as a whole is the body's chemical detoxification system.

theme: Pancreatic and reproductive glandular epithelial development
story: The core is pancreatic development: lineage progression from multipotent progenitors to ductal, NEUROG3+ endocrine and alpha cells, branching morphogenesis and exocrine development. A second block covers reproductive glands, including prostate bud formation, branching and acinus morphogenesis, gonadal mesoderm, testis and Leydig cell differentiation, female gonad and vaginal development. Neuroendocrine, lung secretory and glandular epithelial differentiation and transdifferentiation tie these together as one theme of transcriptional programmes that specify secretory gland epithelia.
